results.expectation: Prescribes documenting a contribution model that specifies who can propose, who reviews, and who approves
results.evidence: Who can propose a new component or change?... Who reviews proposals?... Who approves and merges?

results.expectation: Assigns each component a clear owner
results.evidence: Each component must have a named owner — not a committee, a person or small pair

results.expectation: Enumerates the requirements of a self-governing contribution process: proposal format, design rationale, review checklist, and merge criteria
results.evidence: Gate 1: Proposal Format... Gate 2: Design Rationale Review... Gate 3: Review Checklist... Gate 4: Merge Criteria

results.expectation: Attributes compliance problems to ambiguous documentation and says to resolve them at the component definition stage, not after the fact
results.evidence: Resolve Ambiguity at Definition Time, Not After... your compliance problem exists because teams invent workarounds when the documented component doesn't quite fit their use case

results.expectation: Recommends regular audits comparing the design system to what is actually in production
results.evidence: Conduct Regular Production Audits... Quarterly or biannually, audit what's actually shipped
